reading: Apollo is the One beyond polarity, inviting us out of dualism into unity.
Aion is 'that which always is', the playing child within us.
Truth is subtractive: un-forgetting what we always were.
The child is new and always ancient (from the Cratylus).
Falsehood is the sleep of the soul.
In Phaedo 64 philosophers 'forget' that all they do is practise dying.
First stage of the soul: living the death of truth in the body.
Second stage: carrying the light that sets her on the path.
Third stage: touching the immortal and returning to Demeter.
Initiation begins by closing the senses, and from initiation comes pregnancy of the soul.
Leto's first child, born fleeing Lethe, is virtue.
Apollo, the divine light, is born where truth becomes manifest.
Whatever appears is light woven into forms through the Ideas.
Illness is lack of strength, so the post-birth stage of ῥῶσις is its opposite.
'Killed' means put into darkness: ignorance is the soul's death.
The 'manger of the horses' is the manger of the irrational powers.
Biological life is animal strength and the violent struggle of survival.
Life proper is warmed by fire and lit by consciousness.
Truth is often paradoxical because it goes beyond opinion.
Understanding is going with the flow of things, alert like a good general (Cratylus).
Wisdom is being connected with an ever-moving energy (Cratylus).
Knowledge must be given birth in the mind.
Eros is a cosmic current flowing through you.
Freedom has eros inside it: revolutions are made out of love.
Consciousness wants the new and the flow, not stasis (Cratylus).
Resurrection is stepping out of stasis and inertia.
The dyadic mind that must pass through the drama (she attributes it to Proclus).
Our inner tendencies toward externalisation (following Proclus).
The actor makes an ethos by how he plays a role.
Healthy co-existence of all things in proportion.
Justice is what passes through all things, finest and fastest (Cratylus).
Justice is 'through fire', burning: the subtlest fire pervading the cosmos.
Justice is understanding of the just (Cratylus).
Providence is what comes before the intellect; linked to Athena Pronaia.
The One dwells here, everywhere.
Flowers 'run upward': opening toward the light.

parts.meaning: to see with the eyes and to understand

reading: One word bridges the bodily eye and the soul's eye.
Hestia's flame is our essence.
Eternal means always the same, yet each manifestation is never the same.
Fire is in every seed (some etymologise it so).
The Monad remains and distributes itself without being divided.
To exist is to stand under a principle; the One, being the principle, does not exist but is.
Soul is fiery nous that has cooled; separate selves are ice cubes.
The dry soul is the soul not rained upon, warmed by the fire of the Good.
Consciousness is contact with the forms.
To touch the truth is to be set alight by it.
Only a cataloguing label for Aristotle's work placed after the Physics.
Aion, the playing child, is also the field of play.
Character is formed by habit, so law shapes character.
The agora is a place of speech and exchange of ideas, hence ἀγορεύω.
Politics as a passage into the whole (via the Cratylus).
Every experience happens 'within the limit', in the finite, so awakening, which concerns the infinite, cannot be an experience.
Diotima's beauty is without mechanism, form, mode or way; awakening likewise cannot be engineered by method.
The One 'does not mix' with anything, though all is in it.
Kazantzakis' Abyss: that which has no bottom, an approximation of the formless One.
Theatre, beholding and spectator share one root: we come into the divine theatre to be spectators of truth.
The private, self-serving person; English 'idiot' later took the sense of one asleep in λήθη.
The root of seeing becomes vid- in Sanskrit, linking Greek seeing with Indian knowing.
The sparkle of sunlight on the sea, an image of the One's radiance.
The fool is the one asleep in forgetting, like the self-serving ἰδιώτης.
The aura is a fiery flowing emission of the soul beyond the body, a synthesis of flow and heat.
Incense 'reminds' us: a sensible thing that awakens the soul's Mnemosyne.
Sensation as a rushing motion, read through Proclus as motion meeting a still, perceiving position.
Practical wisdom is understanding of motion and flow, the right circular motion of nous; 'not by chance' akin to ὄσφρησις, smell.
The soul's journey home is 'tasty': it is meant to be enjoyed, and nothing is tastier than eudaimonia.
Prayer and aromas lift us; the Hours mark the moment of awakening.
Fullness is linked with purity, and hence with catharsis; its opposite is the insatiable.
Purified senses perceive the 'pulse of Pallas' and the 'vibration of Zeus'.
Gratitude is the γνώμων that leads to the good, hence the key of all virtues.
Philosophy is an erotic longing to unite with wisdom, not to know about it.

parts.meaning: to close the eyes or mouth

reading: Initiation is closing the eyes to phenomena; a mystery is what cannot be said.
Science is standing above and seeing the whole; whatever is not holistic is not scientific.
A method is a guide for walking the road.
Admitting 'I do not know' opens the soul's pores.
A journey is travelling with order (a friend's etymology she repeats).
Each solstice turning releases food for the soul; the closeness of the words is no accident.
Capricorn is the horn of Amalthea, the nourishment of the infant Zeus, our nous.
The daimon is a fiery self-awareness that knows and teaches: the flame you are at your core.
Happiness tied to chance is a wheel that turns and passes.
Plotinus' untrembling eternity; she links the word by anagram to Artemis.
I am present when I stand toward the One.
Eternity is a disposition: the position of Zeus, of spirit, and also a mood.
Time is nous flowing through duality; linked to Κρόνος. She takes this from a source the notes cannot identify.
The Circle of the Other is the theatre of masks and roles.
Essence is the One polarising 'femininely' into being.
Corinth as the 'divine maiden', and its Isthmus as where λόγος is born.
She reads Χριστός with η: the useful human who found their true need and benefits all beings.
Heracles' mother is the moon with strength.
Something is 'lost' in the tilt of the ecliptic.
Three roots of light: sensible, spiritual and uncreated (third root unclear).
The elided form may allow 'know it': know the only thing that exists, the one Self.
To love is to embrace something with warmth and light.
Happiness is the inner divine spark united with the Good.
We carry our purpose inside, as the acorn carries the oak.
Contemplation is seeing the god: Plotinus's View.

parts.meaning: marketplace of goods and ideas, ruled by Hermes

reading: Apollo's voice entering the agora of the many.
Pythagoras's mother's name already signals purity; she was renamed Pythais.
Pythagoras's school was a place of those who hear together.
Mythology is initiation into theology through symbols.
Phenomena are flashes of light born within mind, so consciousness cannot be separated from them.
Mind as a ship, or a wave, on the ocean of the infinite.
A point of view is a degree of view, and that perspective is our destiny.
The hero's journey home is the soul going from duality through the Good to the One; she admits grammarians would contest it.
She links the word pagan to the inner spring of happiness.
The Muses are doorways to essence.
Chanting ὄν lets the N vibrate as the One becoming being.
What is the σύν that makes the all one? Love.
The world is a jewel, beautiful and ruled by harmony and law.
Question, love and research share a root: questioning is erotic.
The eros of the question leads to the all of the answer.
Ethics means habits of energy, habits of consciousness.

parts.meaning: read as easy flow of soul

reading: Virtue is the soul's unobstructed flow, which she attributes to Plato.

parts.meaning: to divide (she links Latin deus, Spanish dios)

reading: Creative consciousness divides into worlds and unifies them back to the source.

parts.meaning: from a root meaning to cut

reading: A crisis is a cut (τομή) in time where new ideas hatch.
As an anagram, ethics is the way home to the inner centre.
The goddess is the one who knows the characters, so she governs ethics.
The first meditation sets a target, like the root of stochastic.
An inner dialogue in which awareness moves through a field of intention.
Insight is conceived in awareness and born as a realisation, the root of concept.
Technique is a way of giving birth.

parts.meaning: the seminal syllable of flow and impulse

reading: Ares is the upward flow, the impulse of birth.
Ares as 'flow toward the One'.
Spring is when the shoot opens the ground, Ares' work.
We are born 'into the contest' of life.
An oath sets a boundary, as Ares fences Olympus.
Olympus as the all-shining divine nature.
Raised Ares becomes a harmoniser who fits opposites together.
The rainbow, symbol of Olympus, contains Ares in its red outer band.
She ties both words to Ares as 'the moment I stand up': how I act.
Force and life are kin: life-force, neither good nor bad in itself.
Vision is an inner projection of light: a phantasm.
Socrates' pun: the body is a tomb, so the cave is a tomb too.
Return is what gives life its flavour.
The 'real' is the world of things, not the true world of essence.
A Hellene is one whose mind is tuned to spiritual light, not an ethnicity.
Apollo slaying Python dissolves what is rotten and false in us.
Pythagoras' name opens with the gate: he is a gate to the divine.
Work is the offspring of love.
Orpheus is the carrier of the flowing light.
Abaris is the weightless teacher who flew on Apollo's arrow.
Mortal is the consumed ('this problem is eating me'); immortal is the imperishable.
Beauty is 'the omega that flows', the Horai.
Pythagoras' father is mind cleansed so that it remembers.
Fate arises when the One divides into shares.
Seeing is knowing (cf. Sanskrit vidyā).
Thanksgiving activates grace.
Gratitude leads the soul toward its entelechy.
The fool is one who has suffered harm.
Losing Ithaca is losing ethics; coming home is regulating the soul.
To be ancient is to stand toward the principles, not to belong to the past.

Her first step holds two opposite movements at once: a new appetite to ask and learn, and the old, rotten chthonic forces (the Python in the mud) still occupying the soul's oracle. Plutarch's gloss supplies the inquiry; reading both senses together is hers.

The second step is manifestation still through something else: signs, synchronicities, a gate into a deeper network of meaning. Plutarch pairs Delios with Phanaios for one group; treating Delios as its own step is her reading. Part of this section is lost in the transcript.
The third step: direct glimpses of the One with no medium, the veil of plurality pierced by light for an instant. Plutarch gives Delios and Phanaios together; she makes them two separate steps.
The fourth step is 'we know being': those who have ἐπιστήμη leave the cave. Audience members added the river Ismenos and ἵστημι / ἐπιστήμη.
The fifth step is the lesche, where initiates gathered (there was one at Delphi): shared dialogue and philosophy for the common good. 'We are a lesche.'

Socrates' first etymology in the Cratylus (medicine) and her first passage, from Pythios to Delios: washing away what we thought we knew and the poles that cause suffering. Health is simplicity; healing starts with the will to change.
The Cratylus' second etymology (mantic) and her passage from Delios to Phanaios: the α removes the many judgements and reveals a simple truth without content, known directly.

The Cratylus' third etymology (archery) and her passage from Phanaios to Ismenios: the archer aims at the ever-changing (ἀεὶ μεταβαλλόμενα) wildness in us, and the will stops changing and holds one target. The transcript loses part of this passage.

The Cratylus' fourth etymology (music) and her passage from Ismenios to Leschenorios: having gone beyond the poles, he returns to move them together into a new unity. She calls it the political step of consciousness.
Apollo takes no pole and no side; when the many are removed the One appears. She makes a verb of it, 'απολώσου', get un-polarised.
Apollo also destroys, but only the useless: a good loss.
Apollo shot the Python with a hundred arrows; 100 is the letter ρ, flow, so stagnant waters must move and healing begins with the will to change.
Being present with the knowing, the seeing and self-knowledge; we are συνειδότες, witnesses of truth.
Beholding contains the god and the goddess: to behold is to see the divine already here, what you are.

parts.meaning: a root of light, as in ἥλιος

reading: Truth is non-sleep and light, and female because it keeps giving birth. The anagram is flagged as unclear in the transcript.
The nine keys of Apollo point to the 'new one': unity regained after harmonising the many.
Mantic comes from divine mania, which she reads not as madness but as the sacred marriage of heart and nous.
The archer's single focus is a dimensionless point, and that focus is being itself.
Harmony is a joining of opposites (with κρᾶσις and μῖξις), not their absence.

The letters of 'health' code five elements with the noetic idea at the stable centre, balancing emotion, body and thought: Apollo's mean. The passage is garbled; it is likely the Pythagorean health pentagram, and the letter-by-letter pairing follows the order in the notes.
Eros joins and fits together, and peace comes from the same root: 'peace and eros are two sides of the same coin'. The verb is garbled in the transcript.
Because ἐρῶ also means 'I say', eros and logos are directly related: both seek the truth of our soul and want to spring from it.
Living in the flow of eros is vigour and health; illness is the lack of that vigour, an inner civil war.
The εὖ δαίμων is the pure, fiery, already-knowing divine spirit we are; eros exists to remind us of it.
